title: Committee of Supply – Head Q (Ministry of Communications and Information)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head Q (Ministry of Communications and Information)

sections.label: Online Safety Bill implementation update
sections.summary: MCI is asked for an update on Online Safety Bill implementation and next steps beyond social media.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: With this understanding, the Online Safety Bill was passed in this House last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI) provide an update on the implementation progress thus far?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: What are MCI's next steps in ensuring the safety of Singapore users beyond social media services?

sections.label: Cyber addiction in Singapore
sections.summary: A member asks whether recent studies show rising cyber addiction and which age groups are more prone.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In a Straits Times article published in October 2014, it was revealed that an online survey conducted across 9,417 respondents in countries like India, Singapore, UK, USA, Germany and France found Singaporeans to be the second-most Internet addicted people in the world.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Since then, I reckon the numbers of cyber addictions are likely on the rise, as Singaporeans in general have experienced longer screen time, having been cooped up at home during the circuit breaker, coupled with more home-based learning through laptops and tablets which are being introduced to our children and with more companies now being more supportive of telecommuting and flexible work arrangements for its employees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I wish to ask, have any recent studies been done if the numbers are indeed on the rise and do we know which age groups are more prone to cyber addictions?

sections.label: ServiceSG centres for seniors
sections.summary: Six ServiceSG centres assist seniors with Government digital services but may not be within easy reach of all residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I am aware that ServiceSG centres have been set up to assist seniors with Government digital services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, there are only six such centres, which may not be within easy reach of all residents.

sections.label: Young adult scam victims
sections.summary: Singapore Police Force data shows young adults aged 20 to 39 made up 53.5% of scam victims cheated of $660.7 million in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: We tend to assume that the vulnerable are the elderly who are digital dinosaurs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: However, according to recent data released by the Singapore Police Force, young adults aged 20 to 39 made up 53.5% of all scam victims who were cheated of $660.7 million in 2022.

sections.label: Children exposed to inappropriate content
sections.summary: Children risk exposure to violence, pornography and extremist propaganda, including a 15-year-old self-radicalised student who planned attacks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: For example, children are at risk of being exposed to inappropriate content, such as violence, pornography, and extremist propaganda.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: We just learnt of the 15-year-old self-radicalised student who wanted to carry out knife attacks and behead non-Muslims in Singapore, as well as becoming a suicide bomber.

sections.label: Government files access for MPs
sections.summary: A member asks if Government will loosen criteria for file requests already conditionally public to researchers, extending them to all sitting MPs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It also shared that for the book in question, the Ministry granted special permission to cite relevant information in some Government files, subject to conditions to do research in the writing of the book.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I find it incongruent that such information on important national policies can be extended to a researcher but not to legislators for whom the background to policy can be critical.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Would the Government be prepared to loosen its criteria for request to such file, which have already been made conditionally public to others for research purposes to all sitting Members of Parliament?

sections.label: Declassification of government documents
sections.summary: The UK moved to a 20-year rule and Israel to 15 years for most non-security foreign policy documents, prompting a call to declassify documents 25 years from the date of record.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Since then, the UK has completed the transition to a 20-year rule and Israel has moved to a 15-year declassification regime for most of its non-security-related foreign policy documents, while remaining sensitive to its current security situation.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As Mr Low mentioned, we surely are in a better position than Israel.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Thus, it is that we repeat our call for such documents to be declassified, 25 years from the date of record and to make them freely accessible to all.

sections.label: Government advertising spending estimates
sections.summary: MCI estimated Government advertising spend of $150 million to $175 million in FY2019, with increases of 30% to 50% in FY2020 and FY2021, and $50 million to $75 million for the first half of FY2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Responding to a Parliamentary Question posed last year, the Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI) estimated that Government spend $150 million to $175 million in advertising in FY2019, with increases of between 30% and 50% in FY2020 and FY 2021.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: MCI estimated then, for the first half of FY 2022, were between $50 million and $75 million.

sections.label: MCI does not track clicks
sections.summary: The reply to the same Parliamentary Question notes MCI does not track clicks and impressions, as each Ministry is responsible for its own advertising budget and effectiveness.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Additionally, the reply to the same Parliamentary Question above also notes that MCI does not track clicks and impressions as each Ministry is responsible for its own advertising budget and effectiveness.

sections.label: 2022 advertising spending extrapolation
sections.summary: Extrapolating from a Parliamentary Question reply, the Government's total advertising spending in 2022 may have been well over $100 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, extrapolating from a Parliamentary Question reply, the Government's total spending on advertising in 2022 may have been well over $100 million.

sections.label: Advertising and public trust
sections.summary: The speaker suggests ads be run only where there is a measurable behavioural trade-off, with a return on investment test, and that trust cannot be bought with advertising.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If the reply is that such advertising raises public confidence and trust in the agency or Government and hence, conduces more public participation in schemes, surely, the best way to establish trust is good service delivery and surely that trust cannot be bought with advertising.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, as to free up more revenue for the Budget, I would suggest that ads be run only where there is a measurable behavioural trade-off.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A return on investment test should be applied.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Revenue should not be spent on ads that generate "feel good" vibes or which aim to persuade people that the Government is doing a good job.

sections.label: Online news survey findings
sections.summary: In a survey conducted in Singapore from end January to February 2022, 83% of respondents said they get their news online, including through social media.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Based on a survey conducted in Singapore from the end of January to February in 2022, 83% of respondents indicated that they get their news online, including through social media.

sections.label: Supporting vulnerable in digitalisation
sections.summary: The Government must keep support and schemes helping the vulnerable maintain access, get devices, skills and confidence in digitalisation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Some are fearful of being left out or left behind totally.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Hence, as we digitalise, we must continue to help the more vulnerable or less privileged amongst us to: one, maintain access to critical services and information online/offliine; two be empowered with data connection and devices if they wished to go digital; three, be equipped with the right skills; and four, build up confidence in the digital world.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: The Government must continue to make available support and schemes that address these four areas.

sections.label: Pofma responding to falsehoods
sections.summary: Pofma gives the Government the ability to respond to egregious falsehoods against the public interest.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Legislations such as the Protection from Online Falsehoods and Manipulation Act (Pofma) has accorded the Government the ability to respond to egregious falsehoods that are against the public interest.

sections.label: Fight Fake News initiatives
sections.summary: The Government has initiatives such as the Fight Fake News website and S.U.R.E. steps in four languages.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: The Government has several good initiatives such as the "Fight Fake News" website and the Source, Understand, Research and Evaluate (S.U.R.E) steps in four languages.

sections.label: Non-digital essential services
sections.summary: The Government should lead by example to still make essential services available through non-digital means.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: While we should go as far as what the digital world could take us, the Government should lead by example to still make essential services available through non-digital means.

sections.label: IMDA plans for seniors' skills
sections.summary: The question asks what plans IMDA has to further improve the digital know-how and skills of seniors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh
sentences.text: What plans does the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) have to further improve the digital know-how and skills of the seniors?

sections.label: Human connection for seniors' digitalisation
sections.summary: The question asks if SG Digital Office and IMDA will connect at a human level and apply hawker digitalisation to more heartland shops.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In the process of allowing seniors to go digital, may I ask if the SG Digital Office and IMDA will continue to connect at a human level to ease and smoothen the digital transformation for our seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The initiative by the SG Digital Office to allow hawkers to go digital is an important aspect of this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Would MCI and IMDA consider how this can apply to a larger number of shops and small businesses in the heartlands?

sections.label: Digital for Life partnerships
sections.summary: The Government is asked how it enhances partnerships with people, private and public sectors to scale digital inclusion through Digital for Life.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: I have been fortunate to engage with the Digital for Life partners and I am heartened to see the Digital for Life's vibrant and diverse ecosystem of partners from the people, and the private and public sectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: But as digitalisation becomes increasingly embedded in our lives, how is the Government enhancing partnerships with the people, and the private and public sectors to enhance the Digital for Life movement to scale digital inclusion to enable the less digitally-savvy to participate digitally in their daily lives and to allow them to take advantage of the opportunities presented?

sections.label: Bukit Batok East digital programmes
sections.summary: Partners and grassroots organised laptop donations, a coding programme and a carnival bringing IMDA mobile data plans to seniors and special needs community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: They made friends with a few DfL partners and have since brought back ideas to Bukit Batok East (BBE) and worked with some partners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I had received a kind donation of laptops from Tian Kong and Kancanarama Buddhist Temple and we worked with Byte, a DfL partner, to organise a Byte Void-Deck Technology Lab (VDTL) Coding Programme for young children at Bukit Batok East (BBE).

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: My grassroot leaders also organised an Inclusive Family Carnival and brought in IMDA so that seniors and those in the special needs community could get access to mobile data plans as part of the Data for All initiative.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In observing the engagements, I note that there is a need to use different modalities for different demographics and to tier the empowerment strategies to fit the various levels of capabilities.

sections.label: Digital for Life progress and programmes
sections.summary: The passage asks about Digital for Life's progress and next steps, and notes NEU PC Plus and Home Access programmes help lower-income children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The Digital for Life movement is a great effort and platform that can bring Singaporeans from all ages and all walks of life to embrace digital learning as a lifelong pursuit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I would therefore like to ask about the progress of the DfL movement so far.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: What is next and what can we look forward to in doing more so that no one is left behind?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The new NEU PC Plus Programme and Home Access programme ensure that children from lower-income families are not disadvantaged and have access to digital hardware and home broadband.

sections.label: Tech firms retrenching Singaporean workers
sections.summary: A Straits Times report states technology firms laid off 1,270 resident Singaporean workers between July and mid-November 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: According to a Straits Times news report, technology firms laid off 1,270 resident Singaporean workers between July and mid-November 2022.

sections.label: Technology adoption and digital divide
sections.summary: Adoption of artificial intelligence, robotics and machine learning will cause structural unemployment and deepen the digital divide between young and old, haves and have nots.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: At the workplace, the adoption of artificial intelligence, robotics and machine learning technologies will unfortunately translate into structural unemployment for segments of our economy as jobs that have been around for generations get relegated to the history books.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Technological disruptions often exacerbate the digital divide, thereby further deepening the rifts between the young versus the old, the haves versus the have nots.

sections.label: IT skills as core skill
sections.summary: A good command of IT skills is fast becoming a core skill employers look out for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Increasingly, a good command of IT skills is fast becoming a core skill employers look out for.

sections.label: SME digitalisation adoption and MCI plans
sections.summary: Only 19% of companies in the National Business Survey listed Digital Transformation as a top five priority, and the passage asks how well SMEs have adopted digitalisation and what MCI and IMDA are doing in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Yet, only 19% of our companies in the National Business Survey have listed "Digital Transformation" as one of their top five priorities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How well have our SMEs adopted digitalisation and what else is MCI and IMDA doing in 2023 to further drive digital transformation, especially amongst our SMEs?

sections.label: 5G coverage implementation update
sections.summary: The passage asks for an update on 5G coverage implementation and whether it could be expedited, noting a report that nationwide coverage is on track by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Last year, Senior Minister of State Janil reported at the COS that we are on track for nationwide 5G coverage in Singapore by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Could we get an update on the implementation of 5G coverage and if it could be expedited so that Singapore can capture the value created with 5G sooner?

sections.label: Digitalisation progress of businesses and SMEs
sections.summary: The passage asks about the progress of digitalisation of businesses in Singapore, especially amongst SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: What is the progress of the digitalisation of businesses in Singapore, especially amongst SMEs?

sections.label: Digital Connectivity Blueprint development
sections.summary: MCI will develop a Digital Connectivity Blueprint, which may be a world first, if not one of very few.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To this end, MCI will develop a Digital Connectivity Blueprint, which may be a world first, if not one of very few.

sections.label: Digital Enterprise Blueprint development
sections.summary: To strengthen support for businesses, a Digital Enterprise Blueprint will be developed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To strengthen support for businesses, we will develop a Digital Enterprise Blueprint.

sections.label: DigitalAccess@Home scheme for households
sections.summary: A new DigitalAccess@Home scheme starts in April, with about $80 million over four years to support 60,000 households, reducing broadband to as low as $5 per month for eligible HDB rental households.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To that end, we will introduce a new DigitalAccess@Home scheme from April this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Government has set aside about $80 million over the next four years to fund this scheme, which will be able to support 60,000 households.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Under this scheme, the cost of broadband will be reduced to as low as $5 per month for eligible households living in HDB rental flats under the Public Rental scheme.

sections.label: ComCare beneficiaries subsidy qualification
sections.summary: Households with ComCare Assistance beneficiaries automatically qualify for the highest subsidy level and pay the least.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In addition, households which include ComCare Assistance beneficiaries will automatically qualify for the highest level of subsidy and pay the least.

sections.label: DigitalAccess@Home scheme subsidies
sections.summary: Under DigitalAccess@Home, beneficiaries get subsidies of 25% to 75%, paying $75 to $250 for a tablet and $220 to $710 for a laptop.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Under the DigitalAccess@Home scheme, beneficiaries can enjoy subsidies of between 25% and 75%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Depending on the level of support, beneficiaries will pay between $75 and $250 for a tablet, and between $220 and $710 for a laptop.

sections.label: New Digital Access@Home programme funding
sections.summary: The Government will allocate about $80 million over four years for the new Digital Access@Home programme to support low-income households' broadband and device access.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: However, the Government believes that we can do more.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Therefore, we will allocate about $80 million over the next four years to introduce the new Digital Access@Home programme to better support low-income households with access to broadband and digital devices.

sections.label: Seniors' digital proficiency rise
sections.summary: The percentage of seniors in their sixties with basic or higher digital proficiencies rose from 28% to 44%, an increase of 16%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The percentage of seniors in their sixties who have basic or higher digital proficiencies has risen from 28% to 44% – an increase of 16%.

sections.label: Code For Fun and digital movement
sections.summary: Since 2020 Code For Fun has been available to all upper primary students, reaching 50,000 in 2022, and the 2021 movement has over 130 partners and 140 initiatives benefiting over 270,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: For example, since 2020, MOE and IMDA have made Code For Fun, an enrichment programme on Computational Thinking available to all upper primary students.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This is an important social leveller that reached 50,000 students in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Since the movement was launched in 2021 to mobilise ground-up efforts, more than 130 partners have pledged support and kickstarted around 140 initiatives.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: More than 270,000 have benefited from these initiatives.

sections.label: New Code of Practice for App Stores
sections.summary: In response to Ms Tin Pei Ling's and Ms Janet Ang's questions, a new Code of Practice for App Stores will strengthen online safety.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To Ms Tin Pei Ling's and Ms Janet Ang's questions, we will take another step to strengthen online safety through a new Code of Practice for App Stores.

sections.label: Cloud services and data centres
sections.summary: CSA has identified cloud services and data centres as foundational digital infrastructure needing better protection.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Specifically, CSA has identified cloud services and data centres as foundational digital infrastructure we need to better protect.

sections.label: Cybersecurity ecosystem development
sections.summary: CSA is examining developing the cybersecurity ecosystem from talent to innovation, with updates later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: CSA is hence examining how we can develop our entire cybersecurity ecosystem, ranging from nurturing talent to promoting innovation and capability development.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We will provide updates on this as well as the Cybersecurity Act review later this year.

sections.label: AI Verify launch
sections.summary: Last year AI Verify was launched as the world's first AI Governance Testing Framework and Toolkit.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Last year, we also launched AI Verify, the world's first AI Governance Testing Framework and Toolkit.

sections.label: Children's data protection requirements
sections.summary: They must obtain parental consent before collecting data from children under 13 and implement protective defaults.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: For instance, they must obtain parental consent before collecting data from children under the age of 13 and implement protective defaults such as making sure that children's profiles are not made public.

sections.label: Youth news consumption survey
sections.summary: An MCI survey showed 82% of 15- to 24-year-olds regularly consumed local mainstream news online in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: An MCI survey showed that 82% of 15- to 24-year-olds regularly consumed local mainstream news via online platforms in 2021, a jump of around 30-percentage points since 2018.

sections.label: International digital partnerships
sections.summary: Positioning as a thought leader enables partnering like-minded countries and shaping international digital norms through listed initiatives.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In addition, by positioning ourselves as a thought leader, we are better able to partner like-minded countries and shape new international norms in digital.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Promising developments include our chairmanship of the United Nations Open-Ended Working Group on ICT Security, the Digital Economy Agreements with Australia, the UK and South Korea, or the US-Singapore Partnership for Growth and Innovation, the Smart City Initiative with Shenzhen, the ASEAN Data Management Framework which we initiated and the Digital Forum of Small States (Digital FOSS) which we championed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: These initiatives are opportunities for our voice to be heard and our economic space to expand.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: There are no guarantees that we will succeed in every project, nor can we be sure that global developments will always be favourable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: But our foundations are strong, and our investments will bear fruit.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Working with our partners at home and abroad, I am confident we can empower Singaporeans to thrive in our digital future.

sections.label: National Broadband Network investment
sections.summary: The Government invested in the NBN, rolling it out from 2008 and reaching nationwide fibre coverage by 2013, with 98% of households on broadband.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The Government therefore invested in the NBN to provide the high-speed connectivity required to support these services for the betterment of Singaporeans’ lives.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We began rolling out the NBN in 2008 and provided nationwide fibre coverage to homes by 2013.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Today, one gigabit per second plans are the standard among households and 98% are on broadband.

sections.label: 5G roll-out progress
sections.summary: IMDA confirmed 95% nationwide outdoor coverage on Singapore's first two 5G standalone networks, with focus now on industry use.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: To Ms Tin Pei Ling’s question on the progress of the 5G roll-out and development of use cases, the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) had recently measured to confirm that we have reached 95% nationwide outdoor coverage on Singapore’s first two 5G standalone networks.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: With the roll-out progressing well ahead of schedule, our focus is currently on supporting the industry to tap on 5G’s capabilities to enhance their operations and service offerings.

sections.label: Hyundai 5G mobile robots
sections.summary: Hyundai Motor Group's upcoming facility will use over 100 mobile robots, with 5G enabling real-time data transmission for new manufacturing processes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Unlike the fixed production lines in traditional manufacturing, Hyundai Motor Group’s upcoming facility will have over 100 mobile robots deployed across the factory floor to simultaneously transport material required for vehicle manufacturing. 5G is what enables seamless real-time data transmission between the back-end automated control system and the robots. 5G makes possible new manufacturing processes that will both enhance productivity and quality control.

sections.label: Weston Robot river cleaning vessel
sections.summary: Weston Robot's electric Unmanned Surface Vessel uses 5G for video analytics and data throughput to detect and clean rubbish autonomously.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Another newly-awarded project is Weston Robot’s electric Unmanned Surface Vessel for autonomous river cleaning. 5G enables the video analytics and high data throughput necessary for the vessel to detect and clean rubbish outside of its pre-programmed path, and to respond to emergency situations such as oncoming boats.

sections.label: Advisory Panel on Digital Infrastructure
sections.summary: A newly set up Advisory Panel on Digital Infrastructure, co-chaired by the speaker and Mr Irving Tan, is shaping the Digital Connectivity Blueprint.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Shaping the Digital Connectivity Blueprint alongside the Government is a newly set up Advisory Panel on Digital Infrastructure that I co-chair with Mr Irving Tan who has rich experience in the tech sector.

sections.label: 10 gigabits per second upgrade
sections.summary: A full-scale upgrade will deliver speeds of up to 10 gigabits per second, ten times faster than today.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: As announced last year, we will be embarking on a full-scale upgrade to deliver speeds of up to 10 gigabits per second, which is 10 times faster than today.

sections.label: 5G rollout and 6G research
sections.summary: While rolling out 5G networks, Singapore is already embarking on research into next-generation communications technologies like 6G.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: While we roll out our 5G networks, we are already embarking on research into the next generation of communications technologies like 6G.

sections.label: RIE 2025 research talent plans
sections.summary: Under RIE 2025 plans, three areas will be strengthened, starting with expanding research talent, including a call for AI Investigatorships.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Under the Government's Research, Innovation and Enterprise (RIE) 2025 plans, we will strengthen our research and innovation ecosystem in three areas: first, by expanding our base of research talent.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: For example, the Smart Nation and Digital Government Office is partnering the National Research Foundation to launch a call for AI Investigatorships in the coming months.

sections.label: Singapore-South Korea AI MOU
sections.summary: In December last year, Singapore and South Korea signed an MOU on AI to facilitate bilateral AI research and information exchange.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: In December last year, Singapore and South Korea signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) on AI, facilitating bilateral AI research and information exchange.

sections.label: Cybersecurity for 16,000 home devices
sections.summary: The solution has been deployed to improve cybersecurity of 16,000 home devices, such as smart sockets in the HDB Punggol Northshore Project.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Their solution has been deployed to improve the cybersecurity of 16,000 home devices, such as smart sockets in the HDB Punggol Northshore Project.

sections.label: Classified file not publicly accessible
sections.summary: The file in question is not available for public access and remains classified.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: To be clear, the file in question is not available for public access and remains classified.

sections.label: Declassification of government records
sections.summary: Metadata of around 780,000 records is on Archives Online, and since 2016 agencies reviewed over 7,000 records, declassifying some 68,000 file records.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The metadata of around 780,000 records are publicly accessible on Archives Online; and this has been increasing over the years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: In addition, since 2016, Government agencies have reviewed more than 7,000 Government records that were not yet declassified.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: This was in response to 2,130 requests by members of the public.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Eighty-three percent of these records have been approved for access.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: In total, some 68,000 file records have been declassified and made accessible to the public.

sections.label: Digital Economy and I&C growth
sections.summary: The Digital Economy has driven strong growth for Singapore, with the I&C sector growing 13.4% in 2021 and 8.6% in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the Digital Economy has generated strong growth for Singapore, in particular, the Information and Communications, or I&C, sector has grown by 13.4% and 8.6% in 2021 and 2022 respectively.

sections.label: InvoiceNow adoption and grants
sections.summary: Since 2019, 55,000 businesses adopted InvoiceNow, saving an average of $8 per invoice replaced, and firms sending 10 or more e-invoices receive a $200 grant.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Since its launch in 2019, 55,000 businesses have adopted InvoiceNow, which saves an average of $8 for each error-prone and time-consuming invoice replaced.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Firms which have sent 10 or more e-invoices using InvoiceNow, will receive a cash grant of $200.

sections.label: SMEs Go Digital programme support
sections.summary: Since 2017, IMDA's SMEs Go Digital programme has supported more than 88,000 SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Since 2017, Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA)'s SMEs Go Digital programme has supported more than 88,000 SMEs.

sections.label: Funding support for eligible SMEs
sections.summary: Eligible SMEs will receive up to 70% funding support.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Eligible SMEs will receive up to 70% funding support.

sections.label: Government support for SMEs
sections.summary: The Government will continue to guide and support SMEs through refreshed IDPs and the Digital Enterprise Blueprint, and safeguard businesses with upcoming Cybersecurity Health Plans.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: The Government will continue to guide and support SMEs in the next bound of the journey through the refreshed IDPs and the Digital Enterprise Blueprint, while helping safeguard your businesses against digital risks with the upcoming Cybersecurity Health Plans.

sections.label: I&C sector employment outcomes
sections.summary: Seven in 10 retrenched I&C locals found another job within six months; the workforce grew 36% from 130,000 in 2017 to around 177,000 in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Seven in 10 of retrenched locals in the I&C sector were able to find another job within six months.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: The sector's workforce has grown 36%, from 130,000 professionals in 2017, to around 177,000 in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: In the first three quarters of 2022, total employment in the sector grew by 13,700, with thousands of vacancies still available.

sections.label: Employer opportunities for graduates
sections.summary: In six months, leading employers committed 500 good opportunities for ITE and polytechnic graduates.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: In just six months, leading employers have committed 500 good opportunities for our ITE and polytechnic graduates.

sections.label: Advertising standards and children
sections.summary: MCI works closely with ASAS, whose Singapore Code of Advertising Practice and Children's Code for F&B guide advertising conduct.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: From MCI's perspective, we work very closely with the Advertising Standards Authority of Singapore (ASAS) which is an industry body that guides how advertising of products should be conducted through the Singapore Code of Advertising Practice (SCAP).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: For example, the Children's Code for Advertising F&B products guides advertisers to avoid promoting unhealthy consumption habits or irresponsibly pressuring children to buy.

sections.label: Government advertising spending
sections.summary: Last year the Government spent between $175 million and $200 million, around 0.2% of total expenditure, on advertising.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Last year, the Government spent between $175 million and $200 million or around 0.2% of total Government expenditure on advertising.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Members may recall the COVID-19 vaccination campaigns, like "Get your shot, Steady Pom Pi Pi" featuring Phua Chu Kang and "Pak Jiam Buay" by our getai celebrities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: We expect Government's spending on advertising to come down after COVID-19.

sections.label: MND publishing BTO facts
sections.summary: MND proactively puts out facts and figures, including BTO launches and median BTO flat prices, so Singaporeans can make informed decisions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: There is a reason why MND proactively puts out facts and figures, including BTO launches, the median prices of BTO flats, so that all Singaporeans, especially young Singaporeans, know about the pipeline of BTO flats coming up and make the best decision that they can, based on available information.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: These ads show factually, for example, the median price of a 4-room BTO flat in a non-mature estate is about $347,000 before grants.

sections.label: Purpose of Government campaigns
sections.summary: Government agency campaigns aim to inform or educate the public and must not be towards a political end.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Campaigns by Government agencies are for the purpose of informing, or educating the public, Government Ministries are mindful that their advertising must not be towards a political end in Singapore and we take this seriously.

sections.label: Channels and KOL advertising
sections.summary: The Government uses online and offline channels, with about half the advertising budget on digital platforms, and engages KOLs or influencers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   The Government uses various online and offline channels to disseminate information to different groups of audience, and about half of the advertising budget is used on digital platforms such as Mothership, SGAG, and other small-scale social media platforms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Many Government agencies will also engage KOLs, or influencers to advertise.

sections.label: Ministry of Education collaboration
sections.summary: One group collaborates with the Ministry of Education through the school system, and a specific enrichment programme has been implemented for some years.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: One group is in collaboration, of course, with the Ministry of Education, through the school system.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I mentioned earlier in my speech that there is a very specific enrichment programme that has been implemented for some years now.

sections.label: Guardrails for government opinion advertising
sections.summary: The passage asks whether there should be guardrails between advertising that changes people's opinion of the Government and advertising that changes consumer behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: It seems to be more aimed at driving people to change their opinion of the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: So, should there not be guardrails between advertising that drives towards changing people's opinion of the Government versus changing certain behaviours on the part of consumers?

sections.label: MND BTO flat advertisements
sections.summary: MND's ads tell Singaporeans facts about upcoming BTO flat launches, including worked examples on applying CPF grants and proximity grants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: On the MND's ads, it is about telling facts to Singaporeans about the BTO flats launches that are coming up, and some have worked examples of how they can apply the CPF grant; how they can use proximity grants when living near the parents – giving them information to make the best decision that they can.

sections.label: Cybersecurity health plan for SMEs
sections.summary: The cybersecurity health plan encourages SMEs to strengthen cybersecurity, and Cyber Essentials and Cyber Trust marks were launched last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: The cybersecurity health plan will go a long way in encouraging SMEs to strengthen the cybersecurity posture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: For example, it launched the Cyber Essentials and the Cyber Trust marks last year to recognise enterprises which have adopted good cybersecurity measures that correspond to their risk profiles.

sections.label: Scheme income criteria confirmation
sections.summary: The passage asks to confirm whether the criteria remain total gross household income of $1,900 and per capita income of $650.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Can I just confirm that the criteria is still the same as the previous rendition of this scheme, which was, I believe, total gross household income of $1,900 and per capita income of $650?

sections.label: NAS file release permission
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the NAS must seek permission from the originating Ministry or may release the file if reasons are legitimate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Would the NAS have to then seek permission from the originating Ministry, or is it at liberty to release that file provided the reasons are legitimate?

sections.label: Household income eligibility criteria
sections.summary: Eligibility is gross household income of $1,900 per month or less, raised to $3,400 for households with school-going children or a person with disability.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In any case, the eligibility criteria is gross household income of less than or equal $1,900 per month.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But if a household has school-going children or a person with disability, we actually bump it up to $3,400.

sections.label: Blocking scam calls and SMSes
sections.summary: Measures include default blocking of spoofed overseas calls since last July and in-network scanning of SMS for malicious URLs, yielding 57 million fewer spoof calls monthly.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Some of the things that we have done include blocking scam calls as well as SMSes.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We have progressively implemented default blocking of overseas calls that are spoofing local numbers – this has been in place since last July – as well as the in-network scanning of SMS content for malicious URLs – links that could be carried within these SMS messages.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Just to give you a sense of the scale of the impact of these measures, just during the time that I took to deliver my COS speech – I believe it was something like 28 minutes – during that time, we would have blocked about 40,000 malicious calls.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: What that means is that each month, we are getting 57 million fewer spoof calls.

sections.label: Government advertising and marketing spending
sections.summary: The Government spends about 0.2% of total expenditure on advertising and marketing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: First, I spoke about the Government spending about 0.2% of our total expenditure on advertising and marketing.

sections.label: Capability Partnership Programme media collaboration
sections.summary: The Capability Partnership Programme, launched in 2018, has benefited around 120 local media firms and over 830 media talents, with a $5 million Virtual Production Innovation Fund receiving over 40 ideas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: One good example is the Capability Partnership Programme (CPP), which was launched in 2018 to facilitate collaboration between our local companies and reputable international media companies to bring "Made with Singapore" content to the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: The CPP has since benefited around 120 local media firms and over 830 media talents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We also supporting our media firms in adopting technologies to raise production capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: I announced the $5 million Virtual Production Innovation Fund last year to encourage innovation and adoption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: As part of the call for proposals, we received over 40 ideas in the recent call for proposal (CFP).
